IB/qib: Remove qpt_mask global

Fixes: 898fa52b4ac3 "IB/qib: Remove qpn, qp tables and related variables from qib"
Reviewed-by: Mike Marciniszyn <mike.marciniszyn@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Dennis Dalessandro <dennis.dalessandro@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Doug Ledford <dledford@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The use of a global variable `qpt_mask` did not support the multiple chip model of the qib driver, leading to potential conflicts and incorrect behavior when multiple devices were in use. This design flaw made it difficult to manage device-specific configurations, as the global state could be inadvertently modified by different parts of the code, resulting in incorrect operation.

Here is the patch:
 extern u32 qib_cpulist_count;
 extern unsigned long *qib_cpulist;

 extern unsigned qib_cc_table_size;

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
extern u16 qpt_mask;
```
Reason:
The global variable `qpt_mask` was used to manage the state of the qib driver, which did not accommodate multiple chip models. This design flaw allowed different parts of the code to modify `qpt_mask`, leading to conflicts and incorrect behavior when multiple devices were in use.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
-extern u16 qpt_mask;
```
Reason:
By removing the global `qpt_mask`, the code now relies on device-specific configurations stored in the device data (dd). This change eliminates the potential for conflicts and ensures that each device can manage its own state independently, thus supporting the multiple chip model correctly.
